title: The Rare-Earth Game
gist: Paywalled teaser: Daniel Gros argues China will probably not impose a rare-earth embargo but will keep the threat alive, while the West will not reach self-sufficiency yet will keep paying for costly capacity duplication and stockpiles; smaller economies' only defense against coercion is diversification.

insights.claim: China will probably not impose a rare-earth embargo, but it will keep the specter of one alive.
insights.speaker: Daniel Gros
insights.so_what: Rare-earth supply risk persists as a geopolitical lever rather than an actual cutoff; price risk premia may stay elevated.
insights.quote: China will probably not impose a rare-earth embargo, but it will keep the specter of one alive.

insights.claim: The West will probably not achieve rare-earth self-sufficiency but will keep trying to reduce vulnerability to a supply shock through expensive capacity duplication and stockpiles.
insights.speaker: Daniel Gros
insights.so_what: Sustained government-backed spending on non-Chinese rare-earth capacity and stockpiles supports Western producers, at high cost.

insights.claim: Mostly the largest economies, especially the EU and US, are implementing concrete economic-security measures, while for smaller economies the only real option to reduce vulnerability to coercion is diversification.
insights.speaker: Daniel Gros
insights.so_what: Smaller economies are likely to pursue multi-sourcing strategies rather than costly onshoring.
insights.quote: For smaller economies, the only real option for reducing vulnerability to bullying and coercion is diversification.
insights.locator: BERLIN—Economic security is top of mind
